themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 54 THIS WEEK, up 608% from the 7.6-per-week baseline—a statistically severe spike (z-score: 5.81) suggesting widespread pavement, pothole, or infrastructure failures across Morningside Heights requiring immediate investigation into what triggered this sudden deterioration.
evidence: 54 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (608% increase)
Z-score of 5.81 indicates statistically severe anomaly
Community Board has standing request for street/infrastructure funding, suggesting chronic baseline issues now acute
reporting_angles: What specific streets are most affected and why did conditions suddenly deteriorate this week?
Interview NYC DOT on response timeline and whether this reflects deferred maintenance or a discrete event (water main break, construction damage, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Animal & Sanitation Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal private property complaints spiked 1900% THIS WEEK (5 complaints vs. 0.2 baseline), paired with dead animals up 1100% last week and rodent complaints up 200%, indicating a potential disease vector or environmental health crisis in the district requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: Unsanitary animal complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% spike, z-score: 10.97)
Dead animal complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
Rodent complaints: 15 last week vs. 5.0 weekly average (200% increase, z-score: 6.67)
Community Board has standing request for animal/pest control funding, identifying this as persistent systemic need
reporting_angles: Is there a specific location or building triggering the spike in animal-related complaints, or is this district-wide?
Interview NYC Department of Health on potential disease risk (rabies, leptospirosis, hantavirus) and whether this signals broader rat infestation spreading from subway/utility corridors

themes_detail.label: Noise & Street Disruption Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped 271% THIS WEEK to 78 complaints from a 21-per-week baseline (z-score: 5.82), suggesting either a major construction project, event, or quality-of-life emergency concentrated in outdoor/commercial spaces that warrants immediate source identification.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 78 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 21 weekly average (271% increase, z-score: 5.82)
Residential noise remains stable at ~140 complaints/week, suggesting outdoor/commercial sources driving spike
OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints also spiked 700% THIS WEEK (6 vs. 0.8 baseline), pointing to exterior/ground-level disturbance
reporting_angles: Identify whether noise spike correlates with new construction permits filed (365 DOB filings in last 90 days, mostly alterations) or a specific event/festival
Map complaint locations to determine if concentrated around Columbia University campus, the Hill Top Apartments ULURP project, or elsewhere

themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Missed garbage collection complaints surged 1500% last week to 8 complaints from a 0.5-per-week average (z-score: 7.5), paired with 6 'outside building' complaints THIS WEEK, signaling potential Sanitation workforce or route disruptions that could trigger secondary health/pest issues.
evidence: Missed collection: 8 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 7.5)
OUTSIDE BUILDING complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 baseline (700% increase, z-score: 7.94)—likely accumulating trash
Community Board has standing budget request for more sanitation trucks and equipment, indicating chronic resource shortage
reporting_angles: Did a Sanitation Department truck break down, route change, or labor shortage trigger collection gaps last week?
Are trash accumulations visible on streets now, and is this creating conditions for rodent attraction (linking to concurrent pest spike)?

themes_detail.label: Emergency Response Team Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team (ERT) complaints jumped 2300% last week to 3 complaints from a 0.1-per-week baseline (z-score: 8.69), an exceptionally rare type of 311 complaint that typically signals public safety incidents or police/fire deployment warranting investigation into what emergency events occurred.
evidence: Emergency Response Team complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
ERT is a rare complaint type, suggesting unusual incidents when it appears at all
No media coverage or Reddit discussion available, indicating potential reporting gap
reporting_angles: Cross-reference NYPD/FDNY incident reports from last week to identify what emergency deployments triggered ERT 311 complaints
Determine whether complaints relate to fire, police action, or medical emergencies and assess if pattern indicates broader public safety concern
